critique: The title, instruction line, START button, snowy slope, skier, trees, flags, and small HUD are present, and the limited blue-white-red palette commits to a retro game identity. However, the large centered title card occupies the main playfield and visually separates the skier from the slope preview; the tiny skier and scattered props do not yet create an exciting downhill glimpse. Several lines and labels are too fine to feel authentically pixel-built. The trade-off is to preserve the clean cartridge-era framing without allowing the menu panel to suppress the promised skiing scene.
suggestion: Keep the blue pixel border and palette, but shrink and lift the title panel into the upper third, making START the clear red primary action while leaving more visible slope below. Enlarge the skier and create a readable downhill path using staggered trees, gates, tracks, and one expressive snow spray, all on a consistent pixel grid. Move the instruction line directly beneath START at a legible bitmap size, simplify the tiny footer labels, and standardize every border, shadow, icon, and type treatment to hard pixel steps rather than mixed thin vector lines. Preserve ample snowfield, but use the course rhythm to guide the eye from title to skier.
audit_note: Independent FUSED review of only the task brief and common r0 screenshot; no axis critiques or later outputs were consulted.
